objectives.en: State the qualities of a good questionnaire

narration.en: "You don't waste money on junk food, do you?" Will anyone answer this honestly?
narration.kn: "ನೀವು ಜಂಕ್ ಫುಡ್ ಮೇಲೆ ಹಣ ಹಾಳು ಮಾಡುವುದಿಲ್ಲ, ಅಲ್ಲವೇ?" ಇದಕ್ಕೆ ಯಾರಾದರೂ ಪ್ರಾಮಾಣಿಕವಾಗಿ ಉತ್ತರಿಸುವರೇ?

body.en: The instrument for collecting data is a questionnaire or interview schedule. Questions should be few, short, simple and clear; move from general to specific; avoid leading, ambiguous, double-barrelled and personally embarrassing questions; and avoid calculations.
body.kn: ದತ್ತಾಂಶ ಸಂಗ್ರಹಕ್ಕೆ ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾವಳಿ ಬಳಸುತ್ತೇವೆ. ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳು ಕಡಿಮೆ, ಸರಳ, ಸ್ಪಷ್ಟವಾಗಿರಬೇಕು; ಉತ್ತರ ಸೂಚಿಸುವ ಅಥವಾ ಮುಜುಗರ ತರುವ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳು ಬೇಡ.

title.en: On the board: Fixing a bad question

say.en: Here is a bad question. It asks two things and pushes the answer.
Split it into two short, neutral questions with fixed choices.

text.en: Q1. Does your family use buses?

say.en: These are closed questions: easy to answer and easy to count.

text.en: Closed: fixed choices, easy to count

say.en: An open question lets people answer in their own words, but answers are hard to compare.

text.en: Open: own words, hard to compare

prompt.en: Sort each questionnaire item: is it a good question, or leading, double-barrelled or vague?
prompt.kn: ಪ್ರಶ್ನಾವಳಿಯ ಪ್ರತಿ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಯನ್ನು ವಿಂಗಡಿಸಿ: ಒಳ್ಳೆಯ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಯೇ, ಉತ್ತರ ಸೂಚಿಸುವ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಯೇ, ಎರಡು ವಿಷಯಗಳ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಯೇ ಅಥವಾ ಅಸ್ಪಷ್ಟವೇ?

text.en: How many members are there in your family?
Which fuel do you mainly cook with: LPG, kerosene, firewood or other?
In which year did you pass Class 10?
Don't you think the new bus service is excellent?
Most people support the plastic ban. Do you agree with it?
Do you like tea and coffee?
Is the canteen food cheap and tasty?
Do you earn a good income?

explanation.en: A good question is short, clear and neutral, and asks one thing. Leading questions push towards an answer, double-barrelled ones ask two things at once, and vague words like 'regularly' or 'good' mean different things to different people.

body.en: Closed-ended questions give fixed choices, such as two-way (Yes/No) or multiple choice; they are easy to answer and tabulate. Open-ended questions let people reply in their own words; they give richer answers but are hard to compare.
body.kn: ಮುಚ್ಚಿದ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳು ನಿಗದಿತ ಆಯ್ಕೆಗಳನ್ನು ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ, ತೆರೆದ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಉತ್ತರ ಸ್ವಂತ ಮಾತುಗಳಲ್ಲಿ.

points.en: Two-way and multiple-choice questions are closed
Open questions are hard to analyse

problem.en: Improve the question: "Do you and your family use public transport and do you think fares are too high?"

steps.en: It asks two things at once and leads towards "fares are high".
Split it into two neutral questions.
Q1: Does your family use public transport? (Yes / No). Q2: How do you rate bus fares? (Low / Reasonable / High)

narration.en: Let us work this out together. Improve the question: "Do you and your family use public transport and do you think fares are too high?"
Roll-call quiz. When your roll number is called, give your answer.
narration.kn: ಹಾಜರಾತಿ ರಸಪ್ರಶ್ನೆ. ನಿಮ್ಮ ಕ್ರಮಸಂಖ್ಯೆ ಕರೆದಾಗ ನಿಮ್ಮ ಉತ್ತರ ಹೇಳಿ.

narration.en: Now two exam-pattern questions of the kind asked in the PUC board, CBSE board and CUET.

points.en: A questionnaire should be short, clear and neutral.
Avoid leading, double and embarrassing questions.
points.kn: ಉತ್ತರ ಸೂಚಿಸುವ, ಎರಡು ವಿಷಯದ ಮತ್ತು ಮುಜುಗರದ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳನ್ನು ತಪ್ಪಿಸಿ.

points.en: Closed questions are easy to tabulate; open ones give richer views.
points.kn: ಮುಚ್ಚಿದ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳು ಕೋಷ್ಟಕೀಕರಣಕ್ಕೆ ಸುಲಭ; ತೆರೆದ ಪ್ರಶ್ನೆಗಳು ವಿವರ ನೀಡುತ್ತವೆ.
